Description  of Site  Improvements

The  proposed  project  involves  new  construction  of  a 7,150  square-foot  prefabricated  storage

site. The new  storage  building  is proposed  to measure  approximately  65 feet in width,  110  feet in
length,  and 22 feet in height.  The exterior  design  will  consist  of cornugated  metal  siding  throughout
the exterior  walls,  two  roll-up  doors  oriented  south,  window  openings  along  the northerly  fagade,
and a cornigated  metal  gable  roof  design  to match  those  of existing  structures.  The interior  space
will  consist  of an open  floor  plan  (no interior  partitions)  to maximize  the storage  capacity.

The proposed  building  elevations  depict  a 6-inch  gap between  the structures.  However,  the office
building  is proposed  to be attached  to the new  storage  building  with  structural  grade  straps  and
connecting  braces.  The  structure  will  measure  approximately  22'-8"  in width,  52 feet  in length,
and 14 feet in height.  The  exterior  design  will  incorporate  engineered  wood  siding  on the exterior
walls  and a flat roof  design  with  built-up  theri'noplastic  polyolefin  (TPO)  roofing  membrane.  The
interior  configuration  of  the  new  office  building  will  accommodate  three  office  spaces,  one
conference  room,  a supply  room,  a break  room,  an Internet  Technology  (IT)  room,  and  two
restrooms.  A  recommended  condition  will  require  that  the  exposed  connections  between  the
structures  be concealed  with  the engineered  wood  siding  to match  the material  and design  of the
proposed  office  structure.

The new  structures  are proposed  to be painted  in a combination  of earthtone  colors  including  tan,
brown,  off-white,  and  shades  of grey.  The  proposed  color  scheme  of the  storage  building  will
consist  of a tan color  for the exterior  walls,  the roof  will  be painted  grey,  and the doors  will  be
painted  brown.  The  office  building  is proposed  to be painted  with  an off-white  color  with  grey

waste. The design  of the proposed  enclosure  will  consist  of concreate  maso  unit ("cmu")  block
walls  witli  decorative  metal panel  doors.  Staff recommends  a condition  of approval  requiring  that

Business  Operations

The existingmanufacturingplant  utilizes  two primai'yraw  materials  (sand and soda ash) to develop
sodium  silicate.  As part typical  daily operations,  the sand and soda ash are delivered  by truck or
rail and unloaded  into existing  silos. The raw materials  are then weighed  and fed to the furnace
througli  conveyors  and elevators  and heated to fon'n sodium  silicate.  The silicate  comes out in a
liquid  (molten)  form and is cooled.  The solid silicate  is then shipped  off the site as a solid or is
further processed to make liquid  sodium  silicate. The solid products  are shipped out by rail, truck,
or container  and the liquid  products  are shipped by rail, truck, or drums. In addition  to the furnace,
the plant operates a natural  gas-fired  boiler,  two air compressors,  and several water and sodium
silicate  pumps.  There  are conveyors  and elevators  to move  the solid  products  to storage  and
shipping  areas. There are additional  tanks for liquid  processing  and storing liquid  products.

A maximum  of nine employees  currently  works at the site at any time. Designated  employees  visit
other plant buildings  only intermittently.  On-site  transitions  to/from  various  buildings  are done
either on foot or using forklifts  or amaintenance  cart. Theplant  currently  operates Monday  through

maximum  of nine (9) employees  work at the site. The remainer  of the year the plant runs 24 hours,
seven days per week. During this half of the year the plant operates with only four to five (4-5)
employees per working shift. On average, there is one (1) visitor per day to this plant.
